subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue relying on per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This chooses a public config and security boundary for automated jobs, and repository policy treats new config/default surfaces and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive maintainer decisions.

options.title: Add dedicated cron policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as an additive operator-wide policy with documented precedence over per-job `toolsAllow` and no silent inheritance surprises.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as subagent-like for tool policy, reducing config surface but coupling two execution modes that may need different defaults.

options.title: Keep per-job controls only
options.body: Leave `payload.toolsAllow` and delivery safeguards as the supported path and close or narrow this request after documenting that product choice.

recommendation.title: Add dedicated cron policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as an additive operator-wide policy with documented precedence over per-job `toolsAllow` and no silent inheritance surprises.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue as an open cron policy decision and has recent cron/config history in the touched path.
